text:
Anya: Heads up — ACME asked for stronger observability tied to billing. Proposed scope: dashboards (cost by model/route), tracing hooks (span tags for model_id, batch_size, customer_id), error analytics (regression alerts). Need launch criteria and tradeoff estimates. cc @Mohit @Sam :eyes:
Mohit: We can add span tags in the runtime fairly cheaply. Main cost is extra metadata + export. Expect ~5-10% CPU overhead if we emit detailed spans for most requests. Need a sampling policy defined first.
Sam: Agree with Mohit. Also need to decide token-level vs request-level traces. Token-level is expensive. Suggest start with request-level sampling: 10% requests, token-level off by default.
Elaine: From ACME: they want per-customer cost breakdown and per-model tail latency. Their asks: daily dashboard, alert when cost increases >20% week-over-week, and ability to inspect traces for specific billing spikes. Retention request: 30 days for traces.
David: Dashboards are easy if we get consistent tags: model, route, customer_id, batch_size. Cost attribution requires token->model mapping (we have cost-mapper in /analytics). Can wire up if spans include token_count and model_id.
Anya: Draft launch criteria: 1) dashboards populated for last 7 days with model/route/customer slices, 2) tracing tags emitted for >=90% of traffic routes, 3) billing attribution validated with 3 pilot customers, 4) canary rollout for 48h with rollback plan. Is that realistic?
Mohit: 90% coverage is optimistic without route pinning. Recommend 80% initial coverage and a task to get to 90% within 2 weeks. 48h canary is fine.
Sam: Need a privacy check: ensure we never store raw token content. Also add opt-out flag for customers who don't want traces.
Elaine: Confirmed ACME will opt-in. Legal checked that customer_id is fine, but token content must be redacted. They want an explicit opt-in toggle.
Mohit: Plan: feature flag + sampling config + span schema. Rough ETA: 2 sprints for runtime changes, 1 sprint infra (export/storage), 1 sprint analytics/dashboarding. We can parallelize some work.
Anya: Risks: trace storage cost and dashboard freshness. David — can you estimate storage delta for a 1% token-level sampling across current token volume (~2T tokens/month)?
David: Quick calc: 1% of 2T tokens = 20B tokens. If we store token-level meta ~50 bytes/token -> ~1TB/month. If we do request-level only (store request metadata + aggregated token_count), that drops to ~100GB/month. So token-level sampling is expensive; prefer request-level unless customer specifically requires token traces.
Sam: :thumbsup: Proposal: default request-level sampling 5% and token-level off. If a customer needs deeper signals, we enable token-level at a higher cost with explicit opt-in.
Mohit: I'll open the PR with the span tag schema and a sample config. Example config in PR: ```trace_sampling:
  request_rate: 0.05
  token_level: false
  customer_opt_in: true
```
Anya: Action items: Mohit — PR + spec; David — detailed cost delta with current S3/pricing numbers; Sam — privacy/redaction checklist and opt-out flow; Elaine — confirm ACME opt-in and pilot dates. Reconvene Thurs 10am for sign-off. Thanks everyone!
